newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sets up new body to protect its seas.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sets up new body to protect its seas.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto set up a national maritime council on Thursday charged with protecting the nation's numerous seaways from environmental and security threats.
Indonesia, which comprises more than 13,000 islands, stretches across the equator in a wide arc that bridges the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

"The main task of the council is to help the president in formulating and deciding on general policies for dealing with maritime problems and Indonesia's borders," Suharto said in a speech after the appointment of the new council's members.
Suharto, who will head the 18-member council, has for 30 years governed the nation of nearly 200 million people.

The new body, whose deputy head is Coordinating Minister of Politics and Security Affairs Susilo Sudarman, also includes Environment Minister Sarwono Kusumaatmadja, Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad and Armed Forces chief General Feisal Tanjung.
"We are aware that the sea has not only economic potential which needs to be developed, but it is strongly linked with the problems of environment and defence and security," Suharto said.
"We need to increase supervision of the various parties which damage our coral reefs. We need to increase our efforts to avoid our seas being used as a waste dump" he said.
"We must protect the potential of our seas from foreign efforts to illegally exploit them," he said.
